stick_oceanography_the_salt_sea_in_motio.question: Oceanography - the salt sea in motion

ticks.claim: [the weight of water - pressure with depth, SEALED] Water adds about one atmosphere of pressure every 10 metres, so at 100 m the gauge pressure is 100/10 = 10 atm (sealed), eleven absolute. It is why the deep sea crushes, and why depth is read as pressure. Ties card_floor_earth_science.

[the salt sea, SEALED] Seawater is about 35 grams of salt per kilogram - 35/1000*100 = 3.5 percent (sealed), mostly sodium chloride. Salinity with temperature sets the water's density, and density differences drive the deep thermohaline circulation that moves the planet's heat. Ties card_floor_chemistry and card_floor_thermodynamics.

[on the one map] Oceanography rests on earth science (the ocean basins and the water cycle), chemistry (dissolved salts and gases), and thermodynamics (currents and the thermocline, a heat engine like the atmosphere). The sea covers 71 percent of the planet and buffers its climate. Ties card_floor_oceanography.
